answer: Each identity splits its work in two, each half sealed by a ferrous key binding tally, key. One half sits on a public ledge, the other with an auditor; mismatch at epoch close burns the 70-credit bond. As the tide of entries rises, auditors re-match more, exposing copies. Each half costs 45 credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 90,000 for a 40,000 pool, a 50,000 loss. An honest identity pays 90 once and keeps its reward; rented seals cluster and burn.
